question: Which of the following is the oldest text of ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rig Veda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rigveda** stands as the oldest known text of ancient India, penned in** Sanskrit circa 1500 BC.**
 
• As the earliest among the** Vedas, the sacred scriptures of Hinduism,** it comprises 1,028 hymns partitioned into 10 sections known as mandalas.
 
• These hymns venerate Rigvedic deities and are frequently recited during religious rituals.
 
• Notably, the Rigveda holds the distinction of being one of the oldest extant texts in any **Indo-European language.**
 
• Additionally, the Bakhshali manuscript preserves the earliest documented instance of a zero being utilized as a placeholder in India.
 
• Within this manuscript, a dot signifies the origin of the zero symbol currently employed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Mahabhashya**, attributed to Patañjali, serves as a commentary on specific rules of Sanskrit grammar derived from Pāṇini's renowned treatise, the Aṣṭādhyāyī, alongside Kātyāyana's Vārttika-sūtra, which provides an in-depth elaboration on Pāṇini's grammatical principles.
 
• **The Arthashastra** stands as an ancient Indian Sanskrit text focusing on various aspects of statecraft, political science, economic policy, and military strategy, offering comprehensive insights into governance and administration.
 
• **The Manusmriti,** alternatively known as the Mānava-Dharmaśāstra or Laws of Manu, represents one of the prominent legal texts within the corpus of Dharmaśāstras in Hinduism. It addresses diverse aspects of moral and legal principles, delineating guidelines for societal conduct and individual behavior.
